transcript.text: Gas oven took ages to light tonight then went WHOOMPH and now the kitchen smells really strongly of gas even though I've turned it off. Is it safe to try again?

No — do not try to light it again. A delayed ignition followed by a “whoomph” means gas likely built up before it ignited, and a continuing strong gas smell could mean gas is still leaking.

Do this now:

1. Turn the oven controls fully off — don’t attempt relighting.
2. Open doors and windows to ventilate if you can do so safely.
3. Do not use anything that could spark: no matches, cigarettes, lighters, electrical switches, plugs, extractor fan, phone charging, or appliances. Don’t turn lights on or off.
4. If the smell is very strong, you hear hissing, or anyone feels dizzy/sick/headachy: leave the house immediately and keep others away.
5. From outside or a neighbour’s phone, call the gas emergency service / your gas supplier.
• UK: National Gas Emergency: 0800 111 999 (24/7)
• If there is immediate danger or fire: 999 / 112.
• For bottled/LPG gas, contact the cylinder supplier/emergency number as well.

Only turn off the gas supply at the meter/cylinder if you already know how and can do it without lingering in a gas-filled kitchen or using anything electrical.

The oven needs checking by a qualified gas engineer before it is used again.
